answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock tokens in a cryptographic vault and burn a fraction proportional to network density. Registering $k$ identities incurs a superlinear stake burning cost scaling as $O(k^2)$, forcing an attacker’s capital efficiency to its nadir. By pruning synthetic clones across the identity orchard through quadratic slashing, economic friction makes coordinated multi-agent spoofing mathematically unviable.
